rationale: The objective is the wall latency of one complete GraphEncoder forward (infer.py:53-58 sync-bracketed timing; original baseline 0.36707 ms on the immutable reference revision). Discovery on the current revision shows the whole forward is one contiguous region on the 'model' boundary: call 80ff8693 (group 1f40997fb4a53f41b9da) containing both MeanSAGE layers, both Linear projections and 15 CUDA kernels on a single stream. Measured decomposition (torch-profiler diagnostics, corroborated by the separately collected nsys run, resources.json): GPU kernel busy ~322.8 us of the 367 us clean wall, i.e. ~44 us (~12%) host-dispatch/launch slack even unprofiled, while the nsys-captured span (1291.6 us, 25% busy fraction) is only a perturbed upper bound on gaps. Within the 322.8 us busy time the scatter-based neighbor aggregation chain dominates: aten::index_add_ atomic scatter 145.2 us (99.0 us in layer 2, 46.1 us in layer 1; indexFuncLargeIndex/ReduceAdd, ~0.7 TB/s effective, ~16 duplicate destinations per node), the message-materializing index_select gathers 89.0 us, zeros_like 4.8 us, clamp_min 2.5 us, div 6.9 us, plus cat copies 12.2 us feeding the projections - together ~248 us (77%) of kernel time, and the layer-2 messages tensor (67 MB) also drives the 97 MB peak allocation. These costs are jointly determined by one algorithmic choice spanning both layers (the clamp_min and unsqueeze groups each contain one call per layer, so a single-layer boundary would split shared groups), and the dispatch slack and cat copy span the whole forward. A single-group or per-layer edit therefore cannot address the dominant cost; the coherent editable boundary is the entire encoder forward, replaced as one whole bundle at the module boundary (no inherited bundles are installed: search.json installed_bundles [], resources.json bundles [], so no inherited required calls constrain composition). Excluded: group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb / call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (project.invoke) is the frozen adapter measurement boundary, and the outer opop::0 record_function wrap (a60da373/9952fea8/ca1f233e) still fires around any replacement; the inner discovery record_function calls are listed as affected because a fused rewrite that bypasses submodules would stop them. Per binding-contract.md, any capture/replay policy must be composed inside the actual adapter invocation, and this selection explicitly declares the whole region replaced so effective composition is judged on the returned output, not per-op counters.
hypothesis: Hypothesis to test: replacing the whole forward inside the 'model' boundary with a mathematically equivalent implementation that (1) computes neighbor mean aggregation without materializing per-edge messages and without global float atomics - e.g. a duplicate-tolerant spmm/CSR or sorted-segment reduction over (destinations, sources), or a fused gather-reduce kernel built at install time - cutting the 145.2 us atomic index_add_ plus most of the 89.0 us gather and 4.8 us zeros_like; (2) folding degree.clamp_min(1) normalization into the reduction or a reciprocal multiply, eliminating the clamp/unsqueeze/div kernels (~9.4 us plus launches); (3) replacing cat+linear with split GEMMs (x @ W[:, :in] + n @ W[:, in:]) eliminating the 12.2 us cat copies; and (4) shrinking the ~44 us clean-run dispatch/launch slack by reducing 15 kernel launches to fewer - will reduce latency_ms from the 0.367 ms original baseline toward roughly 0.22-0.28 ms (~25-35%), with peak allocated bytes falling as the 67 MB message buffer disappears. Numerical risk is low: any reorder of the same FP32 partial sums stays within atol 1e-5 / rtol 1e-4, and index_add_'s atomic accumulation order is itself non-deterministic. Known constraints and unknowns: any CSR/sort or JIT-compile setup must happen at build/install time or be amortized outside the timed boundary, since cross-invocation caching is barred (no cross-invocation state; workload must execute on current inputs each run); cuBLAS efficiency of the split GEMMs ([4096,256]@[256,256] halves) and the per-invocation cost of building sparse structures are unmeasured on this GPU (GPU counters were deliberately not collected), so the kernel-time split between atomics, memory traffic and launch overhead is inferred from durations and grid shapes, not counter evidence. The nsys gap sizes are profiler-perturbed upper bounds; only the clean harness measurement (warmup 3, repeats 15, median) can accept the candidate.
